name: fmap
sig: Functor f => (a -> b) -> f a -> f b
desc: Apply a function to every value inside.
explain: applies a function to every value inside. `fmap (+1) [1,2] == [2,3]`, `fmap (+1) (Just 1) == Just 2`. Laws: `fmap id == id` and `fmap (f . g) == fmap f . fmap g`.

sig: Functor f => a -> f b -> f a
desc: Replace every value inside with a constant. infixl 4.
explain: replaces every value inside with a constant. `0 <$ Just 5 == Just 0`, `'x' <$ [1,2,3] == "xxx"`. `infixl 4`.

name: pure
desc: Wrap a value in the minimal context.
explain: puts a value into the context in the simplest way. `pure 3 :: Maybe Int` is `Just 3`; `pure 3 :: [Int]` is `[3]`.

sig: Applicative f => f (a -> b) -> f a -> f b
desc: Apply a wrapped function to a wrapped value. infixl 4.
explain: "apply". It takes a function inside a context and a value inside a context. `Just (+1) <*> Just 2 == Just 3`. For lists it tries every combination: `[(+1),(*2)] <*> [10,20] == [11,21,20,40]`. `infixl 4`.

name: liftA2
sig: Applicative f => (a -> b -> c) -> f a -> f b -> f c
desc: Lift a two-argument function into the context.
explain: lifts a two-argument function into the context. `liftA2 (+) (Just 1) (Just 2) == Just 3`.

sig: Applicative f => f a -> f b -> f b
desc: Run both, keep the right result. infixl 4.
explain: runs both, keeps the right result. `Just 1 *> Just 2 == Just 2`, but `Nothing *> Just 2 == Nothing`. `infixl 4`.

sig: Applicative f => f a -> f b -> f a
desc: Run both, keep the left result. infixl 4.
explain: runs both, keeps the left result. `Just 1 <* Just 2 == Just 1`. `infixl 4`.

sig: Monad m => m a -> (a -> m b) -> m b
desc: Bind: feed the result into a function choosing the next action. infixl 1.
explain: bind. It takes the result of the first action and feeds it to a function that chooses the next action. `Just 3 >>= \x -> Just (x * 2) == Just 6`; `Nothing >>= f == Nothing`. Every `do` block is turned into `>>=` calls. `infixl 1`.

sig: Monad m => m a -> m b -> m b
desc: Sequence, discarding the first result. infixl 1.
explain: runs the first, ignores its result, runs the second. `putStr "a" >> putStr "b"`. `infixl 1`.

name: return
desc: Same as `pure`. Does NOT exit the function.
explain: identical to `pure`. Despite the name it does **not** exit the function; it only wraps a value.

name: fail
desc: Called on a failed pattern match in `do`. Maybe gives Nothing, list gives [], IO throws.
explain: called automatically when a pattern on the left of `<-` in a `do` block does not match. For `Maybe` it gives `Nothing`, for lists `[]`, and in `IO` it throws an exception.

name: fold
sig: (Foldable t, Monoid m) => t m -> m
explain: combines all elements with their Monoid. `fold ["ab", "cd"] == "abcd"`. Not exported from the Prelude; `import Data.Foldable (fold)`.

name: foldMap
sig: (Foldable t, Monoid m) => (a -> m) -> t a -> m
desc: Map each element to a Monoid and combine.
explain: turns each element into a Monoid value, then combines them. `foldMap show [1,2,3] == "123"`.

name: foldMap'
sig: (Foldable t, Monoid m) => (a -> m) -> t a -> m
explain: a strict version of `foldMap`. In `Data.Foldable`.

name: foldr
sig: Foldable t => (a -> b -> b) -> b -> t a -> b
desc: Right fold: foldr f z [a,b,c] = f a (f b (f c z)). Can work on infinite lists.
explain: right fold. `foldr f z [a,b,c] = f a (f b (f c z))`. It can work on infinite lists when `f` is lazy in its second argument.

name: foldr'
sig: Foldable t => (a -> b -> b) -> b -> t a -> b
explain: a strict right fold. In `Data.Foldable`.

name: foldl
sig: Foldable t => (b -> a -> b) -> b -> t a -> b
desc: Left fold: foldl f z [a,b,c] = f (f (f z a) b) c. Builds thunks; prefer foldl'.
explain: left fold. `foldl f z [a,b,c] = f (f (f z a) b) c`. It builds up unevaluated thunks; prefer `foldl'`.

name: foldl'
sig: Foldable t => (b -> a -> b) -> b -> t a -> b
desc: Strict left fold; constant space. In the Prelude since GHC 9.10.
explain: the strict left fold. It forces the accumulator at each step, so it runs in constant space. `foldl' (+) 0 [1..1000000]`. It has been exported from the Prelude since GHC 9.10, which is why it is not qualified here.

name: foldr1
sig: Foldable t => (a -> a -> a) -> t a -> a
desc: Right fold seeded with the last element. Crashes on empty.
explain: a right fold with no starting value; it uses the last element as the seed. Crashes on an empty container.

name: foldl1
sig: Foldable t => (a -> a -> a) -> t a -> a
desc: Left fold seeded with the first element. Crashes on empty.
explain: a left fold that uses the first element as the seed. Crashes on an empty container.

name: toList
explain: turns the container into a list. `toList (Just 3) == [3]`. In `Data.Foldable`.

name: null
explain: is it empty? `null [] == True`, `null Nothing == True`.

name: length
explain: number of elements. Trap: `length (1, 2) == 1`, because a pair is Foldable over its second component only.

name: elem
sig: (Foldable t, Eq a) => a -> t a -> Bool
explain: membership. `elem 3 [1,2,3] == True`. `infix 4`.

name: maximum
sig: (Foldable t, Ord a) => t a -> a
explain: the largest element. Crashes on empty.

name: minimum
sig: (Foldable t, Ord a) => t a -> a
explain: the smallest element. Crashes on empty.

name: sum
sig: (Foldable t, Num a) => t a -> a
explain: adds all elements. `sum [] == 0`.

name: product
sig: (Foldable t, Num a) => t a -> a
explain: multiplies all elements. `product [] == 1`.

name: traverse
sig: (Traversable t, Applicative f) => (a -> f b) -> t a -> f (t b)
desc: Map an effectful function and collect the results.
ex: traverse (\x -> if x > 0 then Just x else Nothing) [1,2] == Just [1,2]
explain: maps an effectful function over the container and collects the results. `traverse (\x -> if x > 0 then Just x else Nothing) [1,2] == Just [1,2]`; a single `Nothing` makes the whole result `Nothing`.

name: sequenceA
sig: (Traversable t, Applicative f) => t (f a) -> f (t a)
explain: swaps the layers. `sequenceA [Just 1, Just 2] == Just [1,2]`; `sequenceA [[1,2],[3]] == [[1,3],[2,3]]`.

name: mapM
sig: (Traversable t, Monad m) => (a -> m b) -> t a -> m (t b)
explain: `traverse` with a `Monad` constraint, kept for history. `mapM Just [1,2] == Just [1,2]`.

name: sequence
sig: (Traversable t, Monad m) => t (m a) -> m (t a)
explain: `sequenceA` with a `Monad` constraint. `sequence [Just 1, Nothing] == Nothing`.
combine. `"ab" <> "cd" == "abcd"`, `[1] <> [2] == [1,2]`. Must satisfy `(x <> y) <> z == x <> (y <> z)`. `infixr 6`.

name: sconcat
explain: combines a non-empty list. Not exported from the Prelude; in `Data.Semigroup`.

name: stimes
sig: (Semigroup a, Integral b) => b -> a -> a
desc: Combine a value with itself n times. Import `Data.Semigroup`.
explain: combines a value with itself `n` times. `stimes 3 "ab" == "ababab"`. In `Data.Semigroup`.

name: mempty
explain: the identity element. `mempty :: String == ""`, `mempty :: [Int] == []`.

name: mappend
explain: the old name for `<>`. Same behaviour.

name: mconcat
explain: combines a whole list. `mconcat ["a", "b", "c"] == "abc"`.
equal. `infix 4`.
not equal. Haskell writes `/=`, not `!=`. `infix 4`.

name: compare
explain: returns `LT`, `EQ` or `GT`. `compare 1 2 == LT`.
less than. `infix 4`.
less than or equal. `infix 4`.
greater than. `infix 4`.
greater than or equal. `infix 4`.

name: max
explain: the larger. `max 3 7 == 7`.

name: min
explain: the smaller. `min 3 7 == 3`.

name: minBound
explain: the smallest value. `minBound :: Int == -9223372036854775808`, `minBound :: Bool == False`.

name: maxBound
explain: the largest value. `maxBound :: Int == 9223372036854775807`, `maxBound :: Char == '\1114111'`.

name: succ
explain: the next value. `succ 'a' == 'b'`. Crashes on `maxBound` for bounded types.

name: pred
explain: the previous value. `pred 10 == 9`.

name: toEnum
explain: an `Int` to a value. `toEnum 65 :: Char == 'A'`.

name: fromEnum
explain: a value to its `Int` position. `fromEnum 'A' == 65`, `fromEnum True == 1`.

name: enumFrom
explain: what `[x ..]` means. `[1 ..]` is infinite.

name: enumFromThen
explain: what `[x, y ..]` means. `[1, 3 ..]` is all odd numbers.

name: showsPrec
desc: Precedence-aware show; adds parentheses when needed.
explain: precedence-aware showing; adds parentheses when the context needs them. This is why `show (Just (-3)) == "Just (-3)"`.

name: show
explain: converts to a `String`. `show 42 == "42"`, `show "hi" == "\"hi\""`.

name: showList
desc: How a list of this type shows; Char overrides it so strings show as "abc".
explain: how a list of this type is shown. `Char` overrides it so `show "abc"` gives `"\"abc\""` instead of `"['a','b','c']"`.

name: readsPrec
explain: the old-style parser. The `Int` is the precedence of the surrounding context (0 to 11), which decides whether parentheses are needed. `(readsPrec 0 "5 x" :: [(Int, String)]) == [(5, " x")]`.

name: readList
desc: How a list of this type parses.
explain: how a list of this type is parsed. Exists so `String` can be read as `"abc"` rather than `['a','b','c']`.

name: readPrec
explain: the newer parser interface. Not exported from the Prelude; in `Text.Read`.

name: readListPrec
explain: the newer list parser. In `Text.Read`.
addition. `infixl 6`.
subtraction. `infixl 6`.
multiplication. `infixl 7`.

name: negate
explain: negation. The syntax `-x` means `negate x`.

name: abs
explain: absolute value. `abs (-3) == 3`.

name: signum
desc: Sign: -1, 0 or 1. abs x * signum x == x.
explain: the sign: `-1`, `0` or `1`. The law is `abs x * signum x == x`.

name: fromInteger
explain: how integer literals work. Writing `5` really means `fromInteger 5`, which is why `5` can be an `Int`, a `Double`, or an `Expr`.

name: toRational
explain: exact conversion. `toRational 0.75 == 3 % 4`.

name: quot
explain: division rounding **toward zero**. `quot (-7) 2 == -3`.

name: rem
desc: Remainder for quot; sign follows the dividend.
explain: the remainder that goes with `quot`; its sign follows the **dividend**. `rem (-7) 2 == -1`.

name: div
explain: division rounding **down** (toward minus infinity). `div (-7) 2 == -4`.

name: mod
desc: Remainder for div; sign follows the divisor.
explain: the remainder that goes with `div`; its sign follows the **divisor**. `mod (-7) 2 == 1`. The law is `div x y * y + mod x y == x`.

name: quotRem
explain: both at once. `quotRem (-7) 2 == (-3, -1)`.

name: divMod
explain: both at once. `divMod (-7) 2 == (-4, 1)`.

name: toInteger
explain: converts to `Integer`.

desc: Division; not for Int (use div). infixl 7.
explain: division. `7 / 2 == 3.5`. It does not work on `Int`; use `div` there. `infixl 7`.

name: recip
explain: reciprocal, `1 / x`. `recip 4 == 0.25`.

name: fromRational
explain: how decimal literals work. Writing `3.5` really means `fromRational (7 % 2)`, which is why `3.5` can be a `Double`, a `Float`, or your own `Expr`.

name: log
explain: natural logarithm (base \(e\)). `log (exp 2) == 2.0`.

name: sqrt
explain: square root. `sqrt 16 == 4.0`.

desc: Power with a floating exponent. infixr 8.
explain: power where the exponent is also floating. `2 ** 0.5 == 1.4142135623730951`. `infixr 8`.

name: logBase
explain: logarithm with a chosen base; the **base comes first**. `logBase 2 8 == 3.0`.

name: sin
explain: sine, in radians. `sin (pi / 2) == 1.0`.

name: cos
explain: cosine, in radians. `cos 0 == 1.0`.

name: tan
explain: tangent, in radians. `tan 0 == 0.0`.

name: asin
explain: inverse sine. `asin 1 == 1.5707963267948966` (that is π/2).

name: acos
explain: inverse cosine. `acos 1 == 0.0`.

name: sinh
explain: hyperbolic sine. `sinh 0 == 0.0`.

name: cosh
explain: hyperbolic cosine. `cosh 0 == 1.0`.

name: tanh
explain: hyperbolic tangent. `tanh 0 == 0.0`.

name: asinh
explain: inverse hyperbolic sine. `asinh 0 == 0.0`.

name: acosh
explain: inverse hyperbolic cosine. `acosh 1 == 0.0`.

name: atanh
explain: inverse hyperbolic tangent. `atanh 0 == 0.0`.

name: log1p
desc: log (1 + x), accurate for tiny x. Import `Numeric`.
explain: computes `log (1 + x)` accurately when `x` is tiny. Qualified because the Prelude does not export it; use `import Numeric (log1p)`.

name: expm1
desc: exp x - 1, accurate for tiny x. Import `Numeric`.
explain: computes `exp x - 1` accurately when `x` is tiny. In `Numeric`.

name: log1pexp
desc: log (1 + exp x) without overflow. Import `Numeric`.
explain: computes `log (1 + exp x)` without overflow. In `Numeric`.

name: log1mexp
explain: computes `log (1 - exp x)` accurately. In `Numeric`.

name: properFraction
desc: Whole part and fractional part, same sign.
explain: splits into whole part and fractional part, both with the same sign. `properFraction 3.75 == (3, 0.75)`, `properFraction (-3.75) == (-3, -0.75)`.

name: truncate
explain: rounds toward zero. `truncate (-2.7) == -2`.

name: round
explain: rounds to the nearest whole number, and **ties go to the even neighbour** (banker's rounding). `round 2.5 == 2`, `round 3.5 == 4`, `round (-2.5) == -2`.

name: ceiling
explain: rounds up. `ceiling 2.1 == 3`.

name: floor
explain: rounds down. `floor (-2.1) == -3`.

name: floatRadix
explain: the base of the representation. `2` for `Double`.

name: floatDigits
desc: Mantissa digits: 53 for Double, 24 for Float.
explain: digits in the mantissa. `53` for `Double`, `24` for `Float`.

name: floatRange
explain: lowest and highest exponent. `(-1021, 1024)` for `Double`.

name: decodeFloat
desc: Mantissa m and exponent e with x == m * 2^e.
explain: splits into mantissa `m` and exponent `e` so that `x == m * 2^e`. `decodeFloat 1.0 == (4503599627370496, -52)`.

name: encodeFloat
explain: the inverse. `encodeFloat 1 10 == 1024.0`.

name: exponent
explain: the exponent when the mantissa is scaled into [0.5, 1). `exponent 8.0 == 4`, because `8 = 0.5 * 2^4`.

name: significand
explain: that scaled mantissa. `significand 8.0 == 0.5`.

name: scaleFloat
explain: multiplies by `2^n` cheaply. `scaleFloat 3 1.0 == 8.0`.

name: isNaN
desc: Not a number? NaN is not equal to itself.
explain: is it "not a number"? `isNaN (0 / 0) == True`. NaN is not equal to itself, so `x == x` is False for NaN.

name: isInfinite
explain: `isInfinite (1 / 0) == True`.

name: isDenormalized
explain: is it a subnormal number (extremely close to zero, with reduced precision)?

name: isNegativeZero
explain: `isNegativeZero (-0.0) == True`, even though `-0.0 == 0.0` is True.

name: isIEEE
desc: Follows IEEE 754? True for Float and Double.
explain: does the type follow the IEEE 754 standard? True for `Float` and `Double`.

name: atan2
desc: Angle of point (x, y); Y FIRST; quadrant-correct.
explain: the angle of the point (x, y) from the positive x-axis, correct in all four quadrants. Note the order: **y first**. `atan2 1 (-1) == 2.356194490192345` (3π/4).

desc: Index from 0, O(n); crashes out of range. infixl 9.
explain: list indexing, starting at 0. `[10,20,30] !! 1 == 20`. It walks the list, so it costs O(n). It crashes on a negative or too-large index. `infixl 9`.

desc: Application with lowest precedence (infixr 0); removes parentheses.
explain: plain function application with the lowest possible precedence (`infixr 0`). It exists to remove parentheses: `negate $ 2 + 3` means `negate (2 + 3)`. It can also be passed as a function: `map ($ 3) [(+1), (*2)] == [4,6]`.

desc: Strict application: forces the argument to WHNF first. infixr 0.
explain: strict application. It evaluates the argument to WHNF *before* calling the function. Used to stop unevaluated thunks piling up in accumulators. `infixr 0`.

desc: AND, lazy in the second argument. infixr 3.
explain: logical AND. It is lazy in its second argument, so `False && undefined == False`. `infixr 3`.

desc: OR, lazy in the second argument. infixr 2.
explain: logical OR, lazy in its second argument. `True || undefined == True`. `infixr 2`.

desc: Append; O(length of left list). infixr 5.
explain: appends two lists. `[1,2] ++ [3] == [1,2,3]`. It copies the left list, so it costs O(length of the left list). `infixr 5`.

desc: Composition; right-hand function runs first. infixr 9.
explain: function composition. `(f . g) x = f (g x)`; the right-hand function runs first. `infixr 9`.

sig: Functor f => (a -> b) -> f a -> f b
explain: infix `fmap`. `(+1) <$> Just 2 == Just 3`. `infixl 4`.

sig: Monad m => (a -> m b) -> m a -> m b
explain: bind with the arguments flipped. `f =<< m` is `m >>= f`. Example: `print =<< getLine`. `infixr 1`.

sig: (Num a, Integral b) => a -> b -> a
explain: power with a non-negative whole-number exponent. `2 ^ 10 == 1024`. A negative exponent is a runtime error. `infixr 8`.

sig: (Fractional a, Integral b) => a -> b -> a
desc: Power, integral exponent may be negative. infixr 8.
explain: power with any whole-number exponent, including negative; the base must be fractional. `2 ^^ (-1) == 0.5`. `infixr 8`.

name: all
sig: Foldable t => (a -> Bool) -> t a -> Bool
desc: Every element passes? all p [] == True.
explain: does every element satisfy the test? `all even [2,4] == True`; `all p [] == True`.

name: and
explain: are all of them True? `and [True, False] == False`; `and [] == True`.

name: any
sig: Foldable t => (a -> Bool) -> t a -> Bool
desc: Some element passes? any p [] == False.
explain: does at least one element satisfy the test? `any odd [2,3] == True`; `any p [] == False`.

name: or
explain: is any of them True? `or [False, True] == True`; `or [] == False`.

name: appendFile
desc: Append text to a file (creates it if missing).
explain: adds text to the end of a file, creating it if needed.

name: asTypeOf
desc: Returns the first argument; forces it to the second's type.
explain: returns the first argument, but forces it to have the same type as the second. ``read "5" `asTypeOf` (0 :: Int)`` reads an `Int`.

name: break
desc: Split at the FIRST element that passes.
explain: splits the list at the **first** element that passes the test. `break (> 3) [1,2,4,1] == ([1,2],[4,1])`.

name: span
desc: Longest prefix that passes, and the rest. span p == break (not . p).
explain: splits off the longest prefix that passes the test. `span even [2,4,5,6] == ([2,4],[5,6])`. `span p` is the same as `break (not . p)`.

name: concat
explain: flattens one level. `concat [[1],[2,3]] == [1,2,3]`.

name: concatMap
explain: map, then concat. `concatMap (replicate 2) "ab" == "aabb"`.

name: const
explain: ignores its second argument. `const 1 'x' == 1`. Handy as `map (const 0) xs`.

name: curry
explain: turns a function on pairs into a two-argument function. `curry fst 1 2 == 1`.

name: uncurry
explain: turns a two-argument function into a function on pairs. `uncurry (+) (1,2) == 3`.

name: cycle
desc: Repeat a list forever; crashes on [].
explain: repeats a list forever. `take 5 (cycle [1,2]) == [1,2,1,2,1]`. Crashes on `[]`.

name: drop
desc: Remove the first n; never crashes.
explain: removes the first `n` elements. `drop 2 [1,2,3] == [3]`. Never crashes: `drop 5 [1] == []`, and a negative `n` drops nothing.

name: take
desc: Keep the first n; never crashes.
explain: the first `n` elements. `take 2 [1,2,3] == [1,2]`; `take 5 [1] == [1]`. Never crashes.

name: dropWhile
desc: Drop from the front while the test passes.
explain: removes elements from the front while the test passes. `dropWhile (< 3) [1,2,3,1] == [3,1]`.

name: takeWhile
desc: Keep from the front while the test passes.
explain: elements from the front while the test passes. `takeWhile (< 3) [1,2,3,1] == [1,2]`.

name: filter
explain: keeps the elements that pass the test. `filter even [1..6] == [2,4,6]`.

name: either
sig: (a -> c) -> (b -> c) -> Either a b -> c
explain: handles both cases of an `Either`. `either length negate (Left "abc") == 3`, `either length negate (Right 4) == -4`.

name: maybe
desc: Default for Nothing, function for Just.
explain: handles both cases of a `Maybe`: a default for `Nothing`, a function for `Just`. `maybe 0 (+1) (Just 5) == 6`, `maybe 0 (+1) Nothing == 0`.

name: error
desc: Crash with a message and call stack; fits any type.
explain: stops the program with a message and a call stack. Its result type is any `a`, so it fits anywhere.

name: errorWithoutStackTrace
desc: Crash with a message, no call stack.
explain: the same without the call stack.

name: undefined
explain: a placeholder that crashes when evaluated. Every function in your lab skeletons started as `= undefined`.

name: even
explain: `even 4 == True`.

name: odd
explain: `odd 3 == True`.

name: flip
explain: swaps the first two arguments. `flip (-) 1 10 == 9`.

name: fromIntegral
desc: Any whole-number type to any number type.
explain: converts any whole-number type to any number type. The usual fix for `length xs / 2`: write `fromIntegral (length xs) / 2`.

name: realToFrac
desc: Convert between real types, e.g. Float to Double.
explain: converts between real number types, for example `Float` to `Double` or `Int` to `Double`.

name: fst
explain: first component of a pair. `fst (1, 'x') == 1`.

name: snd
explain: second component of a pair. `snd (1, 'x') == 'x'`.

name: gcd
explain: greatest common divisor, always non-negative. `gcd 12 18 == 6`; `gcd 0 0 == 0`.

name: lcm
explain: least common multiple. `lcm 4 6 == 12`.

name: getChar
explain: reads one character from standard input.

name: getLine
explain: reads one line from standard input, without the newline. Used in your Tic Tac Toe `takeTurn`.

name: getContents
explain: reads all of standard input, lazily (as it is needed).

name: interact
desc: Pass all stdin through a function and print the result.
explain: passes all of standard input through a function and prints the result. `interact (map toUpper)` (with `toUpper` from `Data.Char`).

name: putChar
explain: prints one character.

name: putStr
explain: prints a string **without** a newline.

name: putStrLn
explain: prints a string followed by a newline.

name: print
desc: putStrLn . show; print "hi" shows the quotes.
explain: `putStrLn . show`. So `print "hi"` prints `"hi"` **with** the quotes.

name: readFile
explain: reads a whole file, lazily.

name: writeFile
desc: Write a file, replacing its contents.
explain: writes a file, replacing what was there.

name: ioError
explain: throws an `IOError` inside `IO`. `ioError (userError "boom")`.

name: userError
desc: Build an IOError from a message.
explain: builds an `IOError` from a message, to be thrown with `ioError`.

name: head
explain: first element. Crashes on `[]`. Recent GHCs warn about it for that reason.

name: tail
desc: All but the first; crashes on [].
explain: everything except the first element. Crashes on `[]`.

name: init
desc: All but the last; crashes on [].
explain: everything except the last element. `init [1,2,3] == [1,2]`. Crashes on `[]`.

name: last
explain: last element. Crashes on `[]`.

name: id
explain: returns its argument unchanged. `id 5 == 5`.

name: iterate
explain: the infinite list `[x, f x, f (f x), ...]`. `take 4 (iterate (*2) 1) == [1,2,4,8]`. Used in your Maclaurin series to get repeated derivatives.

name: repeat
explain: an infinite list of the same value. `take 3 (repeat 'x') == "xxx"`.

name: replicate
explain: `n` copies. `replicate 3 0 == [0,0,0]`. Your `emptyBoard` uses it.

name: until
desc: Apply f until the test passes.
explain: keeps applying a function until the test passes. `until (> 100) (*2) 1 == 128`.

name: lex
explain: reads one Haskell token, skipping leading spaces. `lex "  foo bar" == [("foo", " bar")]`.

name: lines
desc: Split on newlines; no empty last line.
explain: splits on newline characters. `lines "a\nb\n" == ["a","b"]`; a trailing newline does not produce an empty last line.

name: unlines
explain: joins lines, adding a newline after **every** line, including the last. `unlines ["a","b"] == "a\nb\n"`.

name: words
desc: Split on any whitespace, drop empties.
explain: splits on any whitespace and drops empty pieces. `words "  a  b\n" == ["a","b"]`. Your `parsePosition` uses it.

name: unwords
explain: joins with single spaces. `unwords ["a","b"] == "a b"`.

name: lookup
sig: Eq a => a -> [(a, b)] -> Maybe b
desc: Find a key in a list of pairs.
explain: finds a key in a list of pairs. `lookup 2 [(1,"a"),(2,"b")] == Just "b"`.

name: map
explain: applies a function to every element. `map (*2) [1,2,3] == [2,4,6]`.

name: mapM_
sig: (Foldable t, Monad m) => (a -> m b) -> t a -> m ()
desc: Run an action per element, discard results.
explain: runs an action for every element and throws the results away. `mapM_ print [1,2]`. Your `prettyPrint` uses it.

name: sequence_
sig: (Foldable t, Monad m) => t (m a) -> m ()
explain: runs every action in order and discards the results. `sequence_ [putStr "a", putStr "b"]`.

name: not
explain: logical negation.

name: notElem
sig: (Foldable t, Eq a) => a -> t a -> Bool
explain: the opposite of `elem`. `notElem 4 [1,2,3] == True`.

name: otherwise
explain: literally `True`. It exists so the last guard reads nicely: `| otherwise = ...`.

name: read
desc: Parse; crashes on failure (prefer readMaybe from Text.Read).
explain: parses a string. `read "42" :: Int`. Crashes if parsing fails, which is why the lab used `readMaybe` from `Text.Read` instead.

name: reads
desc: Parse and return the leftover; [] on failure.
explain: a parser that returns the leftover input too. `(reads "12abc" :: [(Int, String)]) == [(12, "abc")]`; gives `[]` on failure.

name: readIO
desc: Parse; failure is an IO exception.
explain: like `read`, but a failed parse becomes an `IO` exception instead of a crash inside pure code.

name: readLn
desc: Read a line and parse it.
explain: reads a line and parses it. `n <- readLn :: IO Int`.

name: readParen
explain: wraps a parser to handle parentheses. With `True` parentheses are required; with `False` they are optional.

name: reverse
explain: reverses a list. `reverse [1,2,3] == [3,2,1]`.

name: scanl
explain: like `foldl`, but keeps every intermediate result. `scanl (+) 0 [1,2,3] == [0,1,3,6]`. The calculus spec suggested it for factorials: `scanl (*) 1 [1..] == [1,1,2,6,24,...]`.

name: scanl1
desc: scanl seeded with the first element.
explain: `scanl` using the first element as the start. `scanl1 (+) [1,2,3] == [1,3,6]`.

name: scanr
explain: like `foldr`, keeping every intermediate result. `scanr (+) 0 [1,2,3] == [6,5,3,0]`.

name: scanr1
desc: scanr seeded with the last element.
explain: `scanr` using the last element as the start. `scanr1 (+) [1,2,3] == [6,5,3]`.

name: seq
desc: Evaluate the first to WHNF, return the second. infixr 0.
explain: evaluates the first argument to WHNF, then returns the second. `seq undefined 1` crashes, but `seq (undefined, undefined) 1 == 1` because a pair is already in WHNF. `infixr 0`.

name: showChar
explain: puts a character in front. `showChar 'x' "yz" == "xyz"`.

name: showString
explain: puts a string in front. `showString "ab" "cd" == "abcd"`.

name: showParen
explain: wraps the output in parentheses when the flag is True. `showParen True (showString "a") "" == "(a)"`.

name: shows
desc: Show a value in front of more text.
explain: shows a value in front of more text. `shows 12 "abc" == "12abc"`.

name: splitAt
explain: splits after `n` elements. `splitAt 2 [1,2,3] == ([1,2],[3])`. `Board.rows` in your Tic Tac Toe uses it.

name: subtract
desc: subtract x y == y - x; use instead of the section (-1).
explain: `subtract x y == y - x`. Needed because `(-1)` is the number minus one, not a section: write `map (subtract 1) [5,6] == [4,5]`.

name: unzip
explain: splits a list of pairs. `unzip [(1,'a'),(2,'b')] == ([1,2],"ab")`.

name: unzip3
explain: the same for triples.

name: zip
desc: Pair up, stopping at the shorter.
explain: pairs up elements, stopping at the shorter list. `zip [1,2,3] "ab" == [(1,'a'),(2,'b')]`.

name: zip3
explain: the same for three lists.

name: zipWith
explain: combines elements pairwise with a function. `zipWith (+) [1,2] [10,20] == [11,22]`.

name: zipWith3
explain: the same for three lists.
